set_aside.subject: R0-12 photo-read failure precedence
set_aside.text: “An unknown, cross-project or hidden read is answered the same way … while a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error”
set_aside.question: When a photo read is both unknown, cross-project, or hidden and its content is undeliverable, which response takes precedence?
options: Return the concealed response without disclosing the storage failure
Specify an authorization-first rule and apply the storage error only to an otherwise deliverable photo
set_aside.default_guess: Authorize and check visibility first; return the explicit storage-unavailable error only for an otherwise authorized, visible photo.

witness.initial: A viewer has no visibility of a progress photo, and that photo's referenced file is missing.
events: The viewer requests the photo binary.
outcomes: The request receives the same concealed response as every hidden photo read.
The request receives the explicit storage-unavailable error because the photo content cannot be delivered.

set_aside.subject: R0-12 classification of undeliverable photo content
set_aside.text: “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error”
set_aside.question: Which concrete failures count as photo content that “cannot be delivered”: missing content, exceeding binary_max_read_bytes, an unlisted detected media type, unreadable or invalid file_ref, transient I/O failure, or every failure after authorization?
options: Normalize every post-authorization photo-delivery failure to storage-unavailable
Apply storage-unavailable only to missing or unreadable storage; treat oversize and unlisted media as policy refusals
Enumerate separate observable failures for storage, size, and media-type rejection
set_aside.default_guess: Normalize missing, unreadable, oversize, unlisted-media, and other post-authorization delivery failures to one explicit storage-unavailable result.

witness.initial: An authorized viewer can see a progress-photo record, but its stored bytes exceed binary_max_read_bytes.
events: The viewer requests the photo binary.
The service detects that the configured read bound would be exceeded.
outcomes: The viewer receives the explicit storage-unavailable error because the content cannot be delivered.
The viewer receives a size or policy rejection because storage itself is available.

set_aside.subject: R0-12 failure after photo streaming begins
set_aside.text: “The portal streams that object through its own boundary” and “a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error”
set_aside.question: If photo storage fails after response streaming has begun, must the portal guarantee an explicit storage-unavailable response with no binary bytes, or may the caller receive partial bytes followed by a transport abort?
options: Validate or buffer enough to guarantee either the complete exact bytes or an explicit error before any bytes are sent
Permit a partial binary response followed by connection failure
Define a distinct observable mid-stream failure
set_aside.default_guess: Guarantee all-or-error delivery so an undeliverable photo yields the explicit error before any binary bytes are sent.

witness.initial: An authorized, visible photo passes initial checks, but its backing file becomes unreadable midway through reading.
events: The storage read fails before the complete object is sent.
outcomes: No photo bytes are exposed and the viewer receives the explicit storage-unavailable error.
The viewer receives a partial file and then a broken connection, with no explicit storage-unavailable response.
witness.observer: The requesting viewer or API client
